sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A slender shrub or tree up to about 8 m, endemic to north-western Viti Levu, Fiji, where it is recorded in wet montane forest at roughly 900–1,180 m. Leaves have three or five leaflets, with the lowest often very small; star-shaped hairs cover young growth and leaf axes. The original account describes small inflorescences, but the sources do not confirm the flower and fruit details shown in the existing plate.

sections.title: Related species
sections.text: Aglaia archboldiana is another Fijian tree in the genus. It is reported from Viti Levu across a broader elevation range and is distinguished by very large compound leaves and light-brown hairs on young parts.
